Announcing it at dinner, in front of everyone, is the tell: this is a declaration, not a conversation request. They need to feel like someone who decides what they believe rather than someone who attends because it is Tuesday.", "pull": {"collapse": "Enforcer", "instinct": "Lay down the rule that this house goes to church together and they are not exempt, which turns a belief question into a power struggle and almost guarantees the faith itself becomes collateral damage."}, "mentorMove": "Separate the question of what they believe from the question of what this family does together, and stay genuinely curious about the first one before touching the second. You can hold a family expectation without demanding they fake conviction.", "holdFirm": ["Your honest questions about belief are welcome and safe in this house.", "The family expectation around attending together is something we work out as a family, not something one dinner announcement dissolves."], "stayFlexible": ["How much space they get to voice doubt, ask hard questions, or sit differently inside the service.", "Whether there is a version of showing up that does not require them to perform belief they do not yet feel."], "forceLevel": {"level": 2, "label": "Questions"}, "script": [{"phase": "Connection", "words": "I am glad you said it out loud instead of just going quiet on me. That took something, and I want you to know I am not going to make you feel stupid for it."}, {"phase": "Curiosity", "words": "What I actually want to understand is what is underneath this. Is it that you think none of it is true? Is it that it feels like going through motions? Is it the specific people or the specific hour on Sunday? I am not asking to argue you out of it, I genuinely want to know where you are."}, {"phase": "Collaboration", "words": "Here is where I land. I am not going to tell you what to believe, because a belief I hand you like a rule is not really a belief. But we are a family that does this together, and that still matters to me, so I want us to figure out what showing up honestly looks like for you right now rather than you just opting out of the whole thing."}, {"phase": "Commitment", "words": "I am holding us to keeping this conversation open, and I am holding you to bringing your real questions here instead of just closing the door. That is a harder thing to do than either of us just digging in, and I think you are up for the harder thing."}], "longGame": "The kids who get to wrestle with what they believe out loud inside the family usually land somewhere more solid than the ones who either fake it to keep the peace or bolt the moment they can. Your job over the next few years is to be the place where the hard questions are safe, so the door stays open long enough for them to find their own answer."}
situation: My kid announced at dinner they are done with church and are not going anymore.
